questions.prompt: Which part of an animal cell contains genetic material and controls the cell's activities?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains the genetic material (DNA) and controls the activities of the cell.

questions.prompt: Where in the cell does aerobic respiration take place?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration takes place in the mitochondria, releasing energy for the cell.

questions.prompt: What is the job of ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are where protein synthesis happens.

questions.prompt: Which of these is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall (plus chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole). Animal cells don't.

questions.prompt: Plant cell walls are made of ___, which strengthens the cell.
questions.explanation: The cell wall is made of cellulose, which strengthens and supports the plant cell.

questions.prompt: In plant cells, photosynthesis takes place in the ___.
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Which statement about prokaryotic cells (like bacteria) is correct?
questions.correct: Their genetic material is not enclosed in a nucleus
wrong: They are much larger than eukaryotic cells
They make up all plant and animal tissue
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic cells are much smaller than eukaryotic cells and their DNA is a single loop, not in a nucleus.

questions.prompt: Small rings of DNA found in some bacterial cells are called ___.
questions.explanation: Plasmids are small rings of DNA found in some prokaryotic cells, separate from the main DNA loop.

questions.prompt: Under a microscope with a magnification of ×1200, a cell's image is 6 mm wide. What is its real width?
questions.explanation: Real size = image size ÷ magnification = 6 ÷ 1200 = 0.005 mm (5 µm).

questions.prompt: Magnification = image size ÷ ___ size.
questions.explanation: Magnification is the size of the image divided by the size of the real object.

questions.prompt: Why can electron microscopes show structures like ribosomes that light microscopes can't?
questions.correct: They have a much higher resolving power
wrong: They only work on living cells
questions.explanation: Electron microscopes have much higher magnification and resolving power, so they show smaller structures in detail.

questions.subtopic: Cell division, mitosis and stem cells
questions.prompt: Put the stages of the cell cycle in order, starting just after a cell has divided.
items: The cell grows and makes more sub-cellular structures
Mitosis: one set of chromosomes is pulled to each end
The cytoplasm and cell membrane divide to form two cells
questions.explanation: The cell grows and copies its structures, the DNA replicates, mitosis separates the chromosomes, then the cell splits in two.

questions.subtopic: Cell division, mitosis and stem cells
questions.prompt: What does the cell cycle (including mitosis) produce?
questions.explanation: Mitosis and cell division produce two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell.

questions.subtopic: Cell division, mitosis and stem cells
questions.prompt: What is a stem cell?
questions.correct: An undifferentiated cell that can become other types of cell
wrong: A cell that has already specialised
A cell found only in plant stems
questions.explanation: Stem cells are undifferentiated: they can make more cells like themselves and differentiate into other cell types.

questions.subtopic: Cell division, mitosis and stem cells
questions.prompt: Where is meristem tissue found in plants?
questions.correct: At the tips of roots and shoots
questions.explanation: Meristem tissue at root and shoot tips can differentiate into any type of plant cell, all through the plant's life.

questions.prompt: Match each process to what it is.
pairs: Net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration
Water moving across a partially permeable membrane from a dilute to a concentrated solution
Movement against a concentration gradient using energy from respiration
questions.explanation: Diffusion and osmosis are passive; active transport moves substances against the gradient and needs energy.

questions.prompt: Which of these does NOT affect the rate of diffusion?
wrong: The surface area of the membrane
questions.explanation: Diffusion rate depends on the concentration difference, the temperature and the surface area of the membrane.

questions.prompt: Root hair cells absorb mineral ions from very dilute solutions in the soil. Which process do they use?
questions.explanation: The ions move from the dilute soil water into the more concentrated cell, against the gradient, so active transport is needed.

questions.prompt: Why does a single-celled organism not need special exchange surfaces?
questions.correct: Its large surface area to volume ratio lets enough substances diffuse in and out
wrong: It doesn't need oxygen or food
Osmosis can't happen in single cells
It divides too quickly to need them
questions.explanation: A single cell has a large surface area compared with its volume, so diffusion across its membrane meets its needs.

questions.prompt: Bacteria multiply by a simple type of cell division called binary ___.
questions.explanation: Bacteria reproduce by binary fission, splitting into two. In good conditions this can happen every 20 minutes.

questions.prompt: Why are Petri dishes and culture media sterilised before use?
wrong: To make the bacteria grow faster
questions.explanation: Sterilising kills unwanted microorganisms so they can't contaminate the culture.

questions.prompt: In school labs, cultures are usually incubated at a maximum of 25 °C. Why?
questions.correct: It reduces the chance of harmful pathogens growing
wrong: It stops the agar from melting
questions.explanation: Keeping cultures at 25 °C or below makes it much less likely that pathogens which grow at body temperature will grow.

questions.prompt: Match each part of a plant cell to its function.
pairs: Controls what enters and leaves the cell
questions.explanation: Each sub-cellular structure has a job; plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole.

questions.prompt: Why do sperm cells contain lots of mitochondria?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration, releasing the energy the sperm cell's tail needs to swim to the egg.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of xylem cells in a plant?
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water and mineral ions up from the roots. Phloem carries dissolved sugars.
